\frac{\alpha^2+\beta^2}{2 \alpha \beta}=\frac{1+1}{2}=1

questions.q: A computer program has two modules $X$ and $Y$ and errors in them occur independently. $X$ has an error with probability 0.1 and $Y$ has an error with probability 0.3 . the probability having error in $Y$ is $P\left(E_2\right)=0.3\because$ Events are independent.

\therefore P\left(E_1 \cap E_2\right)=P\left(E_1\right) P\left(E_2\right)=0.03

Now, probability having error in $X$ only is

(0.1-0.03)=0.07

Probability having error in $Y$ only is

(0.3-0.03)=0.27

It is given that program is crashed, if an error in $X$ causes alone is 0.5 ,
if error in $Y$ causes alone is 0.7 , and if error in both $X$ and $Y$ causes is 0.8 .
So, required probability

\begin{aligned}
& =(0.07 \times 0.5)+(0.27 \times 0.7)+(0.03 \times 0.8) \\
& =\frac{35+189+24}{1000}=\frac{248}{1000}=\frac{31}{125}
\end{aligned}

questions.solution:
Given, initial value of volume, pressure and temperature of an ideal gas in vessel,

V_1=V, p_1=p \text { and } T_1=T

and density of gas $=\rho$
When, $\Delta V$ volume of gas is let out, hence pressure of gas is decreased to $\Delta p$.
Then,

\begin{aligned}
& V_2=V-\Delta V \\
& p_2=p-\Delta p \\
& T_2=T_1
\end{aligned}

By an ideal gas equation,

\begin{array}{rlr}
\frac{p_1 V_1}{T_1} & =\frac{p_2 V_2}{T_2} & \\
\frac{p_1}{p_2} & =\frac{V_2}{V_1} & {\left[\because T_1=T_2\right]} \\
\frac{p}{p-\Delta p} & =\frac{V-\Delta V}{V}=1-\frac{\Delta V}{V} & \\
\frac{\Delta V}{V} & =1-\frac{p}{p-\Delta p} & \\
& =\frac{p-\Delta p-p}{p-\Delta p} & \\
\Delta V & =\frac{-\Delta p V}{p-\Delta p} &
\end{array}

$\therefore$ Mass of released gas $=\rho \Delta V=\frac{\rho \Delta p V}{p-\Delta p} \approx \frac{\rho \Delta p V}{p}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The half life of neutron is 693 seconds. What fraction of neutrons will decay when a beam of neutrons, having kinetic energy of 0.084 $\mathrm{eV}$, travells a distance of $1 \mathrm{~km}$ ?
(mass of neutron $=1.68 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{~kg}$, and $\ln 2=0.693$ )
questions.solution:
Given, the half-life of neutron, $t_{1 / 2}=693 \mathrm{sec}$ Kinetic energy of neutron $=0.084 \mathrm{eV}\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{2} m v^2 & =0.084 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \\
v^2 & =\frac{2 \times 0.084 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}{m} \\
& =\frac{2 \times 0.084 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}{1.68 \times 10^{-27}}=0.16 \times 10^8 \\
v & =0.4 \times 10^4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$
Time taken by neutron to travelled in $1 \mathrm{~km}$,
$t=\frac{1000}{0.4 \times 10^4} \Rightarrow t=0.25 \mathrm{~s}$
By Radioactive Decay's law,
$\begin{aligned}
N & =N_0\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n \Rightarrow \frac{N}{N_0}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n \\
\frac{N_0}{N} & =2^n
\end{aligned}$
Taking log on the both sides, we get
$\begin{aligned}
\ln \frac{N_0}{N}=\ln 2^n & =n \ln 2=\frac{t}{t_{1 / 2}} \ln 2=\frac{0.25 \times 0.693}{693} \\
& =0.25 \times 10^{-5} \quad[\because \ln 2=0.693]
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A uniform sphere of radius $R$ and mass $m$ is placed on an inclined plane which makes an angle $45^{\circ}$ to the horizontal. For which of the following value of coefficient of friction, the sphere rolls without slipping. Select incorrect option.
questions.solution: Given, radius of sphere $=R$ mass of sphere $=m$ and the angle of inclination in inclined plane, $\theta=45^{\circ}$. \text { The linear acceleration of solid sphere is given by } $$ \\ \begin{array}{ll} a=\frac{g \sin \theta}{1+\frac{I}{M R^2}}=\frac{g \sin \theta}{1+\frac{2}{5} M R^2} & {\left[\because I=\frac{2}{5} M R^2\right]} \\ a=\frac{5}{7} g \sin \theta & \end{array} Applying Newton's second law of motion for linear motion of the centre of mass, $m g \sin \theta-f=m a$ \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow f=m g \sin \theta-m a & =m g \sin \theta-m \frac{5}{7} \cdot g \sin \theta \\ & =\frac{2}{7} m g \sin \theta \end{aligned} $\therefore$ Coefficient of friction $\left(\mu_s\right)=\frac{f}{N}=\frac{\frac{2}{7} m g \sin \theta}{m g \cos \theta}$ =\frac{2}{7} \tan \theta To prevent slipping, $\mu_s \geq \frac{2}{7} \tan \theta$ \mu_s \geq \frac{2}{7} \quad\left[\because \tan 45^{\circ}=1\right] Hence, $\frac{3}{7}, \frac{1}{2}$ and $\frac{5}{8}$ are all greater than $\frac{2}{7}$.

When both the terminal of $A$ and $B$ at $5 \mathrm{~V}$ (high), then both diodes become in reverse bias, hence no voltage appears across due to input voltage, therefore the voltage across $R$ appears as $5 \mathrm{~V}$ high due to $V_2$. questions.solution:
Given, length of string, $l=100 \mathrm{~cm}=1 \mathrm{~m}$
Three resonant frequencies are given as $f_1=120 \mathrm{~Hz}, f_2=200 \mathrm{~Hz}, f_3=280 \mathrm{~Hz}\because$ Fundamental frequency $\left(f_0\right)$ is equal to the greatest common factor of $f_1, f_2$ and $f_3$.

$\therefore f_0=$ greatest common factor of $120 \mathrm{~Hz}, 200 \mathrm{~Hz}$ and $280 \mathrm{~Hz}$ i.e., $f_0=40 \mathrm{~Hz}$
Now, we know that, speed of transverse wave is given by $v=2 l f_0=2 \times 1 \times 40=80 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$.
